fields.Front: Which four AWS services did you use at BMO to modernize 20+ legacy APIs into a serverless, event-driven architecture?
fields.Back: AWS Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, and CloudWatch.

fields.Front: What is an Amazon S3 bucket?
fields.Back: A container for objects (data + metadata) in S3. Bucket names must be globally unique across all of AWS, and each bucket lives in one specific region.

fields.Front: What read consistency model does Amazon S3 provide for all requests (since Dec 2020)?
fields.Back: Strong read-after-write consistency for all GET, PUT, and LIST operations, including overwrite PUTs and DELETEs.

The extra latency when Lambda must provision a brand-new execution environment (download code, boot the runtime, run init code) before handling an invocation, instead of reusing an already-warm environment.

fields.Front: What does setting "reserved concurrency" on a Lambda function do?
fields.Back: It caps the maximum number of concurrent executions that function may use, guaranteeing that capacity for it while throttling any invocations above that ceiling.

fields.Front: What is the maximum execution timeout you can configure for an AWS Lambda function?
Name common event sources that can trigger an AWS Lambda function.
fields.Back: API Gateway requests, S3 object events, DynamoDB Streams, SQS queues, SNS topics, EventBridge rules, and scheduled (cron) rules.

fields.Front: In DynamoDB, what does the partition key determine?
fields.Back: It is hashed to decide which physical partition the item is stored on; it's the required part of the primary key used to route every read/write.

fields.Front: In a DynamoDB table with a composite primary key, what does the sort key let you do?
fields.Back: Store and query multiple items that share the same partition key, uniquely ordered/identified by the sort key (e.g., all orders for one customer, sorted by date).

Modeling multiple different entity types in one DynamoDB table using generic/overloaded partition and sort key attributes, so most access patterns are satisfied with a single request, unlike a relational schema's one-table-per-entity approach.

fields.Front: Why might you choose an eventually consistent read instead of a strongly consistent read in DynamoDB?
fields.Back: It costs half the RCUs and gives lower latency/higher throughput; use it when the app can tolerate reading data that might be a moment stale right after a write.

fields.Front: What's the main practical difference between an API Gateway REST API and an HTTP API?
fields.Back: HTTP APIs are lower-latency and cheaper but support a smaller feature set (fewer integration types, no built-in usage plans/API keys, no WAF); REST APIs support the full feature set, including request validation, response caching, WAF, and usage plans.

fields.Front: In API Gateway's Lambda proxy integration, what is the Lambda function itself responsible for that a non-proxy integration would otherwise handle?
fields.Back: Parsing the raw incoming HTTP request and returning a specifically-shaped response object (statusCode, headers, body) — API Gateway performs no request/response mapping for you.

fields.Front: How does API Gateway enforce request throttling by default?
fields.Back: A token-bucket algorithm applied at the account/stage level with a steady-state rate limit and a burst limit; requests beyond that receive an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response.

fields.Front: What's the difference between what CloudWatch Logs and CloudWatch Metrics store?
fields.Back: Logs store raw, timestamped text log events (e.g., a Lambda function's console output); Metrics store numeric time-series data (e.g., invocation count, duration, error count) used for dashboards and alarms.

fields.Front: What does a CloudWatch Alarm do when its watched metric crosses the configured threshold for the set number of evaluation periods?
fields.Back: It changes state (e.g., OK -> ALARM) and can trigger an action, such as publishing to an SNS topic or invoking an Auto Scaling policy.

A setting that keeps a specified number of Lambda execution environments initialized and ready in advance, so those invocations skip cold starts entirely — the main mitigation for cold-start latency, alongside shrinking the deployment package and avoiding heavy init-time work.

An AWS identity with attached permission policies that can be temporarily assumed by a trusted user, service, or account, instead of using long-lived credentials — e.g., a Lambda function's execution role.

fields.Text: At BMO, modernizing 20+ legacy APIs into a serverless, event-driven architecture (Lambda + API Gateway + DynamoDB) achieved a {{c1::80%}} faster runtime.

Ordering common S3 storage classes from hottest/most expensive to coldest/cheapest: {{c1::S3 Standard}} -> {{c2::S3 Standard-IA}} -> {{c3::S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval}} -> {{c4::S3 Glacier Deep Archive}}.
fields.Extra: IA = Infrequent Access. Deep Archive restores can take hours.

fields.Text: In DynamoDB provisioned mode, one {{c1::Read Capacity Unit (RCU)}} provides one strongly consistent read per second for an item up to 4 KB, and one {{c2::Write Capacity Unit (WCU)}} provides one write per second for an item up to 1 KB.
fields.Extra: An eventually consistent read costs half an RCU.

fields.Text: In DynamoDB, a {{c1::Global Secondary Index (GSI)}} can use a different partition/sort key than the base table and supports only eventually consistent reads, while a {{c2::Local Secondary Index (LSI)}} shares the base table's partition key, must be created at table-creation time, and supports strongly consistent reads.
